rows.n: Urea exports of Oman in customs data (7.63 Mt in 2024, CEPII BACI) are 178% of its production in the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (2 Mt of nitrogen in 2024); urea exports converted to nitrogen with the nitrogen content of urea (0.4665, from molar masses), against ammonia production in nitrogen content. Declaration of cargoes of other origins under Oman is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

notes: Two production tables on two bases: ammonia plant output in tonnes of nitrogen (USGS), the feedstock of urea, and urea production in tonnes of product (FAOSTAT), the basis of the trade tables (HS 310210). Urea holds 46.6% nitrogen (from molar masses), so tonnes of nitrogen and tonnes of urea are not interchangeable.

FAOSTAT has no 2023 urea production figure for Oman, Qatar, Egypt, Algeria, Nigeria, Malaysia and 6 other countries, which each exported more than 1 Mt of urea in the customs data for 2024 (the largest exporters first): the urea producers table lists reporting countries only and gives no world total. For 2022 it gives Oman 2.04 Mt, Malaysia 7.58 Mt, Indonesia 7.47 Mt and United States 5.93 Mt.
FAOSTAT's 2024 urea table is not used: it lists 20 countries against 34 for 2023 and has no figure for China.
Urea exports of Iran in customs data fell from 3.77 Mt in 2019 to 0.024 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI). A change in the recorded origin of shipments is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

Urea exports of Oman in customs data (7.63 Mt in 2024, CEPII BACI) are 178% of its production in the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (2 Mt of nitrogen in 2024); urea exports converted to nitrogen with the nitrogen content of urea (0.4665, from molar masses), against ammonia production in nitrogen content. Declaration of cargoes of other origins under Oman is a plausible cause; it is not established here.
